title: Ambassadors who will not bow
source_text: Ἀλλ᾿ οὐδ᾿ ὡς βλαπτομένου τοῦ θεοῦ, ὡς δοκεῖ βλάπτεσθαι ἄνθρωπος ὑπὸ τοῦ καὶ ἄλλῳ παρ᾿ αὐτὸν δουλεύοντος, ἐκκλίνομεν τὸ δουλεύειν ἄλλῳ τινὶ ἢ τῷ θεῷ διὰ τοῦ λόγου αὐτοῦ καὶ τῆς ἀληθείας αὐτοῦ, ἀλλ᾿ ἵνα ἡμεῖς μὴ βλαβῶμεν ἑαυτοὺς χωρίζοντες τῆς τοῦ ἐπὶ πᾶσι θεοῦ μερίδος, ὡς οἰκείως αὐτοῦ τῇ μακαριότητι ζῶντας πνεύματι ἐξαιρέτῳ υἱοθεσίας“· ὅ ἐστιν ἐν υἱοῖς τοῦ ἐν οὐρανοῖς πατρὸς, οὐ λεξείδια ἀλλὰ πράγματα μεγαλοφώνως κατὰ τὸ κρυπτὸν φθεγγομένοις τὸ „Ἀββὰ ὁ πατήρ.“ Λακεδαιμονίων μὲν οὖν οἱ πρέσβεις τὸν Περσῶν βασιλέα. καίτοι προσαναγκαζόντων σφόδρα τῶν δορυφόρων. οὐ προσεκύνησαν φοβούμενοι τὸν ἕνα κύριον αὐτῶν τὸν Λυκούργου νόμον· οἱ δὲ τὴν πολλῷ μείζονα καὶ θειοτέραν πρεσβείαν „ὑπὲρ Χριστοῦ“ πρεσβεύοντες οὔτε τὸν Περσῶν ἄρχοντα οὔτε τὸν Ἑλλήνων οὔτε τὸν Αἰγυπτίων οὔτε τὸν οὑτινοσοῦν ἔθνους προσκυνήσαιεν ἂν, κἂν οἱ δορυφόροι τῶν ἀρχόντων δαίμονες καὶ τοῦ διαβόλου ἄγγελοι προσαναγκάζειν αὐτοὺς ἐθέλωσι τοῦτο ποιεῖν καὶ πείθωσι μακρὰν χαίρειν λέγειν τῷ παντὸς νόμου τῶν ἐπὶ γῆς κρείττονι. κύριος γὰρ τῶν „ὑπὲρ Χριστοῦ“ πρεσβευόντων ὁ Χριστός ἐστιν, ὑπὲρ οὗ πρεσβεύουσιν, ὁ „ἐν ἀρχῇ“ λόγος ὢν καὶ „πρὸς τὸν θεὸν“ ὢν καὶ „θεὸς“ ὤν.
pass_a_gloss: But not as God being harmed (βλάπτω), as a man seems to be harmed by the one serving also another beside him, do we turn away from (ἐκκλίνω) serving another than God through his Word and his Truth (ἀλήθεια), but so that we may not harm ourselves, separating (χωρίζω) [ourselves] from the portion (μερίς) of the God over all, as living in a way akin (οἰκείως) to his blessedness (μακαριότης) by an excellent (ἐξαίρετος) 'spirit (πνεῦμα) of adoption (υἱοθεσία)', which is in sons of the Father in the heavens, uttering (φθέγγομαι) not little words (λεξείδιον) but realities/deeds (πρᾶγμα) loudly (μεγαλοφώνως) in secret (κατὰ τὸ κρυπτόν) the 'Abba, Father'. The ambassadors (πρέσβεις) of the Lacedaemonians did not prostrate before (προσκυνέω) the king of the Persians, though the bodyguards (δορυφόρος) compelled (προσαναγκάζω) very much, fearing (φοβέομαι) their one lord, the law (νόμος) of Lycurgus; but those being ambassadors on the much greater and more divine embassy (πρεσβεία) 'for Christ' would prostrate neither before the ruler (ἄρχων) of the Persians nor of the Greeks nor of the Egyptians nor of any nation whatever, even if the bodyguards of the rulers, demons and angels of the devil (διάβολος), wish to compel them to do this and persuade them to bid a long farewell (μακρὰν χαίρειν λέγειν) to the one stronger (κρείττων) than every law of those on earth. For lord of those being ambassadors 'for Christ' is the Christ, for whom they are ambassadors, being the Word 'in the beginning', and being 'with God', and being 'God'.
pass_b_english: Nor is it as though God were harmed, as a man seems to be harmed by one who also serves another besides him, that we refuse to serve any other than God, through His Word and His Truth. It is so that we may not harm ourselves by separating ourselves from the portion of the God over all, since we live in kinship with His blessedness by the excellent “spirit of adoption.” That spirit is in the sons of the Father in heaven, who cry aloud in secret “Abba, Father” (Romans 8:15), uttering not mere words but realities.

The ambassadors of the Lacedaemonians, though the king’s bodyguards pressed them hard, did not bow down before the king of the Persians, because they feared their one lord, the law of Lycurgus (Herodotus, Histories 7.136). But those who go on the far greater and more divine embassy “for Christ” (2 Corinthians 5:20) would not bow down before the ruler of the Persians, or of the Greeks, or of the Egyptians, or of any nation whatever, even if the bodyguards of those rulers, demons and angels of the devil, should wish to force them to do so, and should try to persuade them to say a long farewell to Him who is greater than every law on earth. For the Lord of those who are ambassadors “for Christ” is Christ, for whom they are ambassadors, who was the Word “in the beginning,” who was “with God,” and who was “God” (John 1:1).

choices.choice: Romans 8:15: πνεῦμα υἱοθεσίας ... Αββα ὁ πατήρ (also Galatians 4:6 for ‘Abba, Father’). ‘Father in heaven’ is the Gospel phrase (e.g. Matthew 6:9), not cited. μεγαλοφώνως κατὰ τὸ κρυπτόν (‘loudly, in secret’) is a deliberate paradox, perhaps recalling Matthew 6:6 (ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ); kept. The Spartan envoys’ refusal of prostration before Xerxes is told in Herodotus 7.136; the idea of law as the Spartans’ ‘master’ comes from Herodotus 7.104 (ἔπεστι γάρ σφι δεσπότης νόμος); Origen calls it ‘the law of Lycurgus’. ‘the angels of the devil’ recalls Matthew 25:41 (τῷ διαβόλῳ καὶ τοῖς ἀγγέλοις αὐτοῦ), not cited inline. τῷ παντὸς νόμου τῶν ἐπὶ γῆς κρείττονι may be masculine (‘Him who is greater’, i.e. Christ, as the next sentence suggests) or neuter (‘that which is greater’); masculine chosen to match the parallel with the Spartans’ ‘one lord’. The orphan closing quotation mark after υἱοθεσίας in the copy-text marks the end of the Romans quotation; the opening mark has dropped out. The potential optative προσκυνήσαιεν ἂν is rendered ‘would not bow down’. οἱ δορυφόροι τῶν ἀρχόντων δαίμονες καὶ τοῦ διαβόλου ἄγγελοι: the bodyguards are themselves the demons and angels of the devil (one group, in apposition), not two groups. πράγματα after λεξείδια rendered ‘realities’ (not ‘deeds’). οἰκείως ... τῇ μακαριότητι rendered ‘in kinship with His blessedness’. ‘spirit of adoption’ and ‘Abba, Father’ are the same verse; cited once, after the second.
bodyguards now one group in apposition: 'the bodyguards of those rulers, demons and angels of the devil' (was split into two groups); Pass A corrected
πράγματα 'deeds' changed to 'realities'; clause moved after 'Abba, Father' for natural order
'in a manner akin to' changed to 'in kinship with' (οἰκείως)

choices.choice: 8.6 τῷ ... κρείττονι: kept the translator's 'Him who is greater than every law on earth' (Christ); the neuter or 'the law greater than every earthly law' reading, which mirrors the Spartans' law, is also possible. Noted in translator_notes; no owner call needed.
